title: Evolution of Benchmark: Black-Box Optimization Benchmark Design through Large Language Model

mechanism.populationDetail: N programs occupy reference-vector slots with local neighborhoods; no persistent islands or tree are described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: A separate Pareto-front set preserves multiple non-dominated benchmark programs across generations.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Generation-level survivor choice compares each offspring with its slot parent and up to two neighboring parents; a separate Pareto archive is then updated.
mechanism.generationDetail: Normal valid pairs undergo true two-parent synthesis; one-invalid pairs use only the valid parent, while double-invalid pairs trigger fresh structural generation.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: PBI scalarizes the LSI/ADC vector for local selection, but both objectives and PBI are exposed to reflection.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Two programs are drawn from a five-neighbor reference-vector neighborhood; validity may reduce their effective contribution to one or zero.
